name: Online Store
description: Customers, orders and products wired together the way a typical storefront is. A good all-round starting point.

name: SaaS Subscriptions
description: Multi-tenant billing: organizations, plans, subscriptions and invoices, with every table hanging off the tenant.

name: Blog & CMS
description: Posts, authors and comments, plus a posts-to-tags junction table — the clearest example of a many-to-many relationship.

name: Project Tracker
description: Projects, tasks, assignees and labels. Close to what an issue tracker stores, including a labels junction.

name: School Management
description: Students, courses and teachers joined through enrollments, with assignments and submissions on top.

name: Clinic & Appointments
description: Departments, doctors, patients and appointments — a chain three levels deep, ending at prescriptions.

name: Library Lending
description: Books, members and loans in five tables. The smallest template here — the whole diagram fits on one screen.

name: Warehouse Inventory
description: Items, suppliers and stock tracked per warehouse, so the same product can sit in several places at once.

name: Social Network
description: Posts, likes and replies — plus a follows table that joins users to users, the self-join people most often get stuck on.

name: HR & Payroll
description: Employees, departments and payslips, with a manager_id pointing back into employees so the reporting line is visible.

name: Restaurant Orders
description: Tables, staff and orders, with menu items built from ingredients through a recipe junction.

name: Music Streaming
description: Artists, albums and tracks, with playlists joined through a table that carries its own data — the track's position.
